emergency.condition_text: a spell or ability on the stack is pointed at one of your permanents
indications: An opponent holds two or more untapped sources through your whole turn and casts nothing
The Ur-Dragon has just resolved and a seat with blue or white mana is still untapped — log 006, where Stephen answered the commander on the turn it landed
Your only cost reducer is on the battlefield and the second is in hand — log 002, where the reducer was answered before the discount engine did anything
You have just cast Twinflame Tyrant, Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm or Panharmonicon into an open table — log 005, where the Tyrant went down before the Dragons and was removed immediately
Lightning Greaves is on the battlefield attached to nothing
immediate: Stop before the spell resolves. Count your untapped lands, your untapped mana creatures and the instants in hand, then decide — log 006 skipped this step with a response available and let the removal resolve.
Tap Bloom Tender or Faeburrow Elder for one mana per colour among your permanents before you decide you cannot pay. With all five colours on your side that is five mana from one creature.
Cast Stubborn Denial for {U} if the spell is noncreature. With a creature of power 4 or greater on your board it counters outright; 21 of the 30 creatures in the 99 have power 4 or greater.
Cast Mithril Coat for {3}. It has flash and attaches on entry to a legendary creature you control; you have twelve of them, the commander included.
Cast Deflecting Swat and send the spell at a token or a mana creature. Check that a commander is on the battlefield first — without one it costs {2}{R}.
subsequent: Equip Lightning Greaves in your precombat main phase, before you cast the Dragon you need to keep. Equip is sorcery speed and cannot be done in response to the answer.
Cast Thunderbreak Regent before the Dragon that matters. Every opponent spell or ability that targets a Dragon you control then deals its controller 3.
Cast Asceticism for {3}{G}{G} once two or more Dragons are down. Hexproof stops every targeted answer at the table and still lets your own Mithril Coat and your own {1}{G} regenerate target them.
Hold Sarkhan's Triumph for the rebuild. It is an instant that puts a Dragon in hand; cast it on the turn after the answer lands, not before it.
emergency.notes: Lightning Greaves grants shroud as well as haste. A Dragon wearing the Greaves cannot be targeted by your own Mithril Coat trigger, by Boros Charm's double-strike mode or by Asceticism's regenerate. Move the Greaves off before the turn you need to target that body. And Mithril Coat answers destruction: exile, bounce and an edict go straight through it.

emergency.condition_text: a sweeper is coming and the board is committed
indications: The pod has wiped on each of the last two nights — log 002 records the cycle as board established, board erased, repeat, and log 006 names Stuart's board wipes
Three or more untapped sources in white or black held through your turn
An opponent who has cast nothing for two turns and is holding four or more cards
Four or more Dragons on your board and no attack made yet
Miirym's token copies on the board — they die with everything else and do not come back
immediate: Count the damage the board already presents. If it kills a seat this turn, attack that seat now instead of adding a Dragon.
Stop deploying at three Dragons and a payoff. Keep the fourth Dragon and the second reducer in hand.
Leave {1}{G}, {2}{W} or {3} untapped across the table's turns, for Heroic Intervention, Teferi's Protection or Mithril Coat.
Cast Flawless Maneuver while a commander is on the battlefield; it costs nothing then.
Cast Heroic Intervention rather than Flawless Maneuver when the board you are saving includes Panharmonicon, Dragon Tempest or Garruk's Uprising. Flawless Maneuver covers creatures.
subsequent: Rebuild to two Dragons and a payoff, not to five bodies.
Cast Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks or Scourge of Valkas before the next Dragon, so the rebuild deals damage as it happens rather than after it finishes.
Cast Atsushi, the Blazing Sky into the next wipe on purpose. Its death trigger is three Treasures or two cards off the top.
Recast The Ur-Dragon only behind a printed reducer.
emergency.notes: Teferi's Protection phases your whole board out until your next turn, so casting it in your own main phase costs you that turn's attack — cast it on an opponent's turn. Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat are free only while a commander is on the battlefield, and the goldfish has The Ur-Dragon on the battlefield by turn six in 0.333 of 10,000 runs; before that they cost {2}{W} and {2}{R}. Indestructible and hexproof both do nothing against exile, bounce or an edict.

emergency.condition_text: the table has read you as the problem and is converging
indications: Your board reads lethal on a seat and you cannot attack until next turn
Somebody has said your damage total out loud — log 003, where the table converged inside one cycle of reading "Sean is swinging for 28 in the air"
You have killed two commanders with entry damage — log 004, where that made you the obvious problem and three players picked you apart inside one rotation
Two opponents have passed a turn cycle without attacking each other
A seat is assembling quietly while the table's removal is pointed at you — log 004: Steven won with a tap/untap engine nobody attacked
immediate: Count what you can kill this turn. If it is not a whole seat, hold the next Dragon and pass with mana up.
Cast Thrakkus the Butcher or Atarka, World Render in the precombat main phase of the turn you attack, never the turn before.
Name a second threat before you pass. Point at one permanent somebody else controls and say what you would spend removal on.
Attack the seat with the most life. Scourge of the Throne's dethrone counter and its extra combat both require it, and it puts your damage where the table already wants it.
Hold Teferi's Protection until a second player commits to you. One removal spell is not the convergence.
subsequent: Cast Whirlwing Stormbrood and deploy at the end of the turn before yours from then on. It gives your sorceries and your Dragon spells flash, so the board arrives after the table has spent its turn.
Rebuild to one Dragon and one payoff, and let the next two turns be somebody else's.
Spend Swords to Plowshares or Generous Gift on the seat that is not attacking you, once, in front of the table.
Attack the quiet assembler once every turn cycle from the moment you name him.
emergency.notes: Log 003's mistake was the order, not the cards: Gadrak, the Crown-Scourge landed a turn before the deck could present lethal, and the table had a full cycle to strip the three artifacts Gadrak needs to attack, fight the Dragons and ping the rest. Deploy the multiplier and the attack on the same turn.

emergency.condition_text: the colours have stopped arriving, or a land-hate effect has taken them
indications: Four or five lands on turn six while the table is on eight or more — log 002
No green source on the battlefield with Farseek, Nature's Lore or a green Dragon in hand — log 005, lost with exactly that hand
Black stranding first: on-curve from lands alone reads 0.524 for black against 0.718 or better for every other colour
Blood Moon or an equivalent resolved — log 001. Seven basics survive it: four Mountain, one Forest, one Island, one Plains, and there is no Swamp in the 99
Your untapped sources are Cavern of Souls, Delighted Halfling, Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon or Unclaimed Territory and the spell in hand is not a creature, a Dragon or a legend
immediate: Play the untapped land that makes the colour you are missing and pay the life. Battlefield Forge, City of Brass, Mana Confluence, Spire of Industry and Sunbaked Canyon all enter untapped and all charge life.

Crack the fetch for a dual rather than a basic and pay the two life. Arid Mesa, Bloodstained Mire, Scalding Tarn and Wooded Foothills each reach several of the ten lands in the 99 that carry a basic type.
Cast Bloom Tender or Faeburrow Elder ahead of any other play at that cost, and play the coloured land before them — each adds one mana per colour already among your permanents.
Point Farseek at Blood Crypt, Overgrown Tomb or Smoldering Marsh. Those are the black sources it reaches, and black is the short colour.
Cast Chromatic Lantern on the turn a colour is actually missing rather than on curve. It turns every land you control into a source of that colour.
subsequent: Under a land-hate lock, play the colourless and red half and pick one seat. Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Talisman of Dominance, Chromatic Lantern, Dragon's Hoard, Herald's Horn, Urza's Incubator, Lightning Greaves, Mithril Coat and Steel Hellkite need no coloured mana at all, and the red Dragons are castable off Mountains.

Cast Skyshroud Claim off five mana rather than a five-drop Dragon. It puts two Forest-typed lands onto the battlefield untapped, and Breeding Pool, Canopy Vista, Cinder Glade, Overgrown Tomb and Stomping Ground all carry the type.
Sacrifice Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon for {4} once you have a spare land drop; it puts a Dragon in hand.
Recast The Ur-Dragon only once a printed reducer is down. Dragonspeaker Shaman and Urza's Incubator each take {2} off it; eminence does not, because eminence discounts other Dragon spells.
emergency.notes: Five sources pay for SPELLS only: Cavern of Souls, Delighted Halfling, Desolation of Smaug, Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon and Unclaimed Territory. Four of them also carry a plain "{T}: Add {C}", which pays a generic cost such as Mithril Coat's {3} equip or Steel Hellkite's {X}; none of them pays a coloured activation such as Asceticism's {1}{G} regenerate or Lathliss's {1}{R}. Count that mana twice before you call a hand castable.

emergency.condition_text: the reducer and the ramp never came together and the table is developing past you
indications: Turn six with no cost reducer on the battlefield — the goldfish draws one by turn six in 0.421 of 10,000 runs, and reducer plus ramp together in 0.337
Two Dragons at mana value five or more in hand on four lands — log 006, where Smaug the Magnificent and Thrakkus the Butcher were kept and neither was cast on time
Your cost reducer was answered and the second is still in hand — log 002, where the discount engine never did its job
The Ur-Dragon still uncast on turn seven: the median cast turn is 7 and it never arrives at all in 2,277 of 10,000 runs
No Treasure source and no per-Dragon payoff on the battlefield
immediate: Cast the cheapest thing that carries a per-Dragon trigger rather than holding for the big one: Dragon Tempest at {1}{R}, then Firespitter Whelp at {2}{R}.
Cast Breaching Dragonstorm or Roiling Dragonstorm for the card rather than for the body. Each returns to your hand when a Dragon you control enters, so it is recastable rather than spent.
Cast Sarkhan's Triumph for the Dragon your mana pays for this turn, not for the biggest one.

Cast Desolation of Smaug for its mana half when you hold a Dragon you cannot otherwise afford: 3 damage to each non-Dragon creature, and four mana in any combination of colours to spend on a Dragon spell.
Cast the cost reducer before the ramp spell when you can only have one.
subsequent: Cast Hellkite Courser for {4}{R}{R} and put The Ur-Dragon onto the battlefield instead of paying nine.
Cast Sneak Attack and put Drakuseth, Maw of Flames in for {R}. Its trigger is on the attack, so all 17 damage lands before the end-step sacrifice.
Cast Garruk's Uprising or Temur Ascendancy before the next Dragon of power 4 or greater, so the rebuild draws as it lands.
Cast Steel Hellkite off six mana of any colours when the coloured Dragons are stranded.
emergency.notes: Hellkite Courser puts The Ur-Dragon onto the battlefield and returns it to the command zone at the beginning of that turn's end step. Neither event is casting, so the commander tax never moves and the next cast is still {4}{W}{U}{B}{R}{G} — stack 008 step 11, on the Courser's official 2020-11-10 ruling. The Courser grants haste to the COMMANDER, not to itself: with no Dragon Tempest, Temur Ascendancy or Lightning Greaves already on the battlefield, the Courser sits out the turn it lands and only the commander attacks. Stack 008 is checker-failed on one citation in step 4 and its four answers do not rest on it; read the page before you run the line.

emergency.condition_text: a seat is assembling a line and you cannot interact with every piece
indications: A seat tutoring twice inside one turn cycle — log 006: Stephen's Sisay is a tutor on a stick for any legendary piece
A seat with an engine on the battlefield that nobody has attacked — log 004: Steven won with a tap/untap engine while the table spent its removal on you
A seat holding mana open every turn and casting nothing
A graveyard filling on the other side of the table
immediate: Say what you have seen. Name the piece to the table so a seat holding an answer has a reason to spend it.
Cast Stubborn Denial for {U} on the noncreature half of the line. With a creature of power 4 or greater on your board it counters outright rather than taxing.
Cast Transcendent Dragon at flash speed for {4}{U}{U}: it counters the spell, exiles it, and lets you cast that spell yourself for nothing.
Spend Chaos Warp or Generous Gift on the piece already on the battlefield. Chaos Warp is an instant and both reach any permanent.
Change target. Attack the assembling seat every turn from here, whatever the arithmetic says about the other two.
subsequent: Keep attacking the same seat after the line is broken once; they reassemble faster than you rebuild.
Cast Sarkhan's Triumph for Drakuseth, Maw of Flames rather than for a value Dragon — the answer to a line you cannot interact with is ending the game first.
Activate Steel Hellkite for {X} equal to the combo piece's mana value on a turn it has dealt that seat combat damage; it destroys each nonland permanent at that mana value they control.
Hold Teferi's Protection for the turn the line goes off, and cast it against damage or drain.
emergency.notes: Teferi's Protection buys one turn cycle against damage and drain and buys nothing against mill, an alternate-win clause, or a lockout that does not target you. Reading every oracle text in the 99, one card mentions a graveyard at all — Transcendent Dragon, exiling the spell it counters. There is nothing to point at a graveyard, so do not spend removal on a creature that comes back; spend it on whatever puts it there.

emergency.condition_text: a seat is on a faster clock than yours and the table is not answering it
indications: An opponent attacking by their fourth turn while your first attack is two turns out
A wide board of small bodies opposite you and no blocker of yours on the ground
Your hand is six-drops and the table is already trading life
Your board power under ten on turn five — the goldfish's mean is 9.755 at turn five and 14.877 at turn six, unopposed and against nothing that blocks
immediate: Cast the cheapest body that blocks and still pays you: Firespitter Whelp at {2}{R}, then Thunderbreak Regent at {2}{R}{R}.
Block with the tokens. Miirym's copies and Lathliss's 5/5s are blockers before they are damage and cost nothing to lose.

Cast Crux of Fate on the non-Dragon mode and accept the price: it also kills Birds of Paradise, Bloom Tender, Delighted Halfling, Faeburrow Elder, Ignoble Hierarch, Dragonlord's Servant, Dragonspeaker Shaman and Solphim, Mayhem Dominus, which are the eight non-Dragon creatures in the 99.

Spend Generous Gift or Chaos Warp on the anchor of the wide board rather than on the biggest single body. Swords to Plowshares gives the racing seat life — save it for the one attacker you cannot block.
Attack the racing seat, not the open one.
subsequent: Cast Smaug the Magnificent or Glorybringer on the turn you need damage now; both have haste.
Cast Twinflame Tyrant before the next Dragon. Every Dragon Tempest and Scourge of Valkas trigger after it deals double.
Equip Lightning Greaves to the first Dragon that lands so it attacks the turn it arrives.
Activate Steel Hellkite for {X} of 0 on a turn it has connected with the racing seat: that destroys every token and every Treasure they control.
emergency.notes: No logged game has ended this way, so this page is reasoned from the list and the model rather than from a night at the table — read it as weaker than the six pages above it. Twinflame Tyrant doubles combat and noncombat damage; Solphim, Mayhem Dominus doubles noncombat damage, so Solphim adds nothing to a swing.

keep: Three lands, one of Birds of Paradise / Bloom Tender / Delighted Halfling / Faeburrow Elder / Ignoble Hierarch, and a cost reducer
Two lands with Sol Ring or Arcane Signet — log 003's turn-one four mana, off the one keep the pilot writes up as the mana working
Three lands, one of Farseek / Nature's Lore / Skyshroud Claim, and a Dragon at mana value five or less
Any hand with Bloom Tender and two green sources
Three lands and two of Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks, Scourge of Valkas, Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm
ship: A hand with no green source — the pilot's own rule after log 005, where Farseek and the green Dragons sat in hand all game
Three lands, one rock and two Dragons at mana value five or more with no cost reducer — log 006's keep, which the pilot does not stand by
A hand whose cheapest spell costs five — log 002's keep, and the mana never arrived
Two lands with no Sol Ring, no Arcane Signet, no Talisman of Dominance and no one-mana mana creature
preflight.note: Mulligan on colours and on the cheapest spell, not on land count. The early land drops hold — 0.891 on turn three — and then fall to 0.756 on four and 0.615 on five, while the reducer-plus-ramp hand assembles in 0.462 of 10,000 runs. The hand you are looking for makes three colours and casts something on turn two.

steps: Play the untapped land on turn one and pay the life if it asks for it.
Cast Sol Ring, Arcane Signet or Talisman of Dominance on turn one ahead of any other play.
Cast the mana creature on turn two, and play a coloured land before Bloom Tender or Faeburrow Elder — both count the colours already among your permanents.
Cast the cost reducer on turn three. Dragonspeaker Shaman and Urza's Incubator each take {2} off a Dragon spell; Dragonlord's Servant and Herald's Horn take {1}.
Point Farseek at the black or blue dual and Nature's Lore or Skyshroud Claim at a Forest-typed dual, and take the colour you are shortest on rather than the land that enters untapped.
startup.note: Eminence discounts other Dragon spells and never The Ur-Dragon itself, so the commander costs nine until a printed reducer is on the battlefield. Dragonspeaker Shaman and Urza's Incubator together take it to five.

steps: Cast the payoff before the Dragon. Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks and Scourge of Valkas all read "whenever a Dragon enters"; a Dragon that lands first is damage you did not deal.
Cast Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm ahead of the expensive Dragon rather than after it. Every nontoken Dragon behind her arrives twice.
Cast Whirlwing Stormbrood once you hold two or more Dragons, and from then on cast your Dragons and your sorceries at the end of the turn before yours.
Cast The Ur-Dragon with a printed reducer already down, or put it onto the battlefield with Hellkite Courser for {4}{R}{R}.
Equip Lightning Greaves to the piece you cannot rebuild — Miirym, or the last reducer — and move it off before the turn you need to target that body.
assembly.note: Hellkite Courser grants haste to the commander it deploys and not to itself, so without Dragon Tempest, Temur Ascendancy or Lightning Greaves already out the Courser sits out the turn it lands. The commander returns to the command zone at that turn's end step whether it attacked or not, and the next cast still costs {4}{W}{U}{B}{R}{G} — nothing here is a cast, so no tax is added.

steps: Count every seat's life at the start of your turn, before you untap.
Leave {U} up for Stubborn Denial from the moment a creature with power 4 or greater is on your board; 21 of the 30 creatures in the 99 qualify.

Stop before any removal spell or ability resolves. Count your untapped lands, your untapped mana creatures and the instants in hand, then let it resolve — log 006 is the game that skipped this with five mana available and a response in hand.
Tap Bloom Tender or Faeburrow Elder for one mana per colour among your permanents. With all five colours out, that is five mana from one creature.
Attack the player with the most life, so Scourge of the Throne's extra combat turns on.
cruise.note: You hold an answer in 0.890 of goldfish runs at turn six and can cast one in 0.510 — the mana to hold a response up arrives later than the response does. Cast the ramp before the protection every time the choice appears.

steps: Count the target seat's life, then count the Dragons you control. Dragon Tempest and Scourge of Valkas each deal that number for every Dragon that enters.
Cast Twinflame Tyrant before the Dragon that carries the trigger. It doubles every point; Solphim, Mayhem Dominus doubles noncombat damage.
Cast Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm, then the Dragon. The copy is a second "enters" for every payoff on the battlefield.
Aim every instance at one seat. Stacks 002 and 007 put that board at 42 damage on a single player by the eighth of twelve instances; split across two seats the same board kills neither.
Attack with Thrakkus the Butcher or Atarka, World Render on the board and Garruk's Uprising down for trample.
closing.note: Token copies do not re-trigger Miirym or Lathliss, so the cascade terminates — stacks 001 and 002 both settle this. Count the nontoken arrivals, not the bodies.

optics: Cast your Dragons and sorceries at the end of the turn before yours once Whirlwing Stormbrood is on the battlefield. A board that appears after the table has spent its turn gives nobody a window to price it.
Cast the reducer before the Dragon. A Dragonlord's Servant reads as a Goblin; a Terror of the Peaks reads as a countdown.
Keep the board at three Dragons until the turn you attack.
Leave one Dragon back untapped. A seat that cannot be attacked profitably is not the seat the table attacks.
Do the arithmetic in your head and say the number out loud on the turn it is lethal — in log 003 the table converged inside one cycle of hearing it.
reveal: Hold Mithril Coat and Stubborn Denial until an answer is on the stack. Both cost less than the turn they save.
Show a protection spell once. A table that has watched Heroic Intervention resolve prices the next wipe differently.
Spend removal on somebody else's threat early, in front of the table, so your own enchantments have a reason to be left alone.
Hold Sarkhan's Triumph until after another seat has tutored.
Keep Teferi's Protection unannounced. It decides whether the convergence works, and it works once.
alliances: Name the other threat before you pass, every turn, and be specific: one permanent, and what you would spend on it.
Take the deal that has you attacking the leader. Scourge of the Throne needs the most-life seat anyway, so the political ask and the mechanical one are the same ask.
Trade one removal spell for a problem that is not yours, early, and say so while you do it.
Hold one Dragon back when two seats ask you to attack the third. Swinging with everything on somebody else's turn plan ends your turn with no blockers.
Attack the seat the table has already named, once per turn cycle, and say that is what you are doing.
targets: Attack the player with the most life first. Dethrone and Scourge of the Throne's extra combat both require it.
Attack the quiet assembler second — log 004: the seat nobody attacked won the game.

Spend Chaos Warp and Generous Gift on an artifact, an enchantment or a land. Swords to Plowshares, Crux of Fate, Glorybringer and Desolation of Smaug reach creatures, and Steel Hellkite reaches a nonland permanent only on a turn it has dealt that player combat damage.
Point Swords to Plowshares at the blocker with flying or reach rather than at the largest attacker. This deck's damage is in the air and its problem is the one body that stops it.
Hold Crux of Fate for a board you are behind on, and read the non-Dragon mode as also killing your five mana creatures, both creature reducers and Solphim, Mayhem Dominus.
